claims.text: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck at 5.5996, 125.0647 (offshore Sarangani, Philippines) on 7 June 2026 at 23:37 UTC, at 35 km depth, generating a maximum tsunami wave of 1.93 metres; GDACS issued an orange alert for medium humanitarian impact with about 2.9 million people exposed to Modified Mercalli Intensity VII or greater.

OCHA's 'Philippines: 7.8 Sarangani Earthquake Response Snapshot' (as of 13 July 2026) reports 94 deaths, 1,316 injured and 18 missing, alongside 391,891 families (1,655,313 persons) affected across 650 barangays and 25,048 families (95,629 persons) still displaced.

DSWD DROMIC Report #75, as of 23 July 2026, 6PM, reports 392,157 families (1,656,596 persons) affected across 661 barangays in Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM (Tulunan, North Cotabato added: 10 barangays, 182 families). Total displaced: 27,118 families (107,475 persons) — 7,592 families (30,889 persons) inside 75 evacuation centers, 19,526 families (76,586 persons) outside with relatives/friends. Houses damaged: 115,205 total (18,644 totally destroyed, 96,561 partially damaged) — revised down from prior reports after data validation and deduplication conducted 21 July 2026. Cost of assistance provided to date: PHP 1,288,971,829.87.

DSWD DROMIC Report #76, as of 24 July 2026, 6PM, reports a total of 392,389 families (1,657,524 persons) affected in 661 barangays in Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM. There are 7,982 families (32,890 persons) currently taking temporary shelter in 85 evacuation centers in Regions XI and XII, and 19,526 families (76,555 persons) temporarily staying with relatives or friends; total displaced stands at 27,508 families (109,445 persons) in Regions XI, XII and BARMM. A total of 115,205 houses were damaged, of which 18,644 were totally damaged and 96,561 were partially damaged, in Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM. A total of ₱1,306,112,420.37 worth of assistance was provided to the affected families, of which ₱1,306,092,420.37 from DSWD and ₱20,000.00 from the LGUs.

Re-checked 1 August 2026: ReliefWeb's disaster page for this earthquake (eq-2026-000083-phl) still lists DSWD DROMIC Report #76 (24 July 2026, 6PM) as the latest DROMIC report, with no #77 or later published; the page's status remains 'Ongoing'. No OCHA casualty figure newer than the 13 July response snapshot (94 deaths, 1,316 injured, 18 missing) has been published.

Re-checked 2 August 2026: DSWD DROMIC Report #76 (24 July 2026) remains the latest in its series, with no Report #77 yet published; the OCHA 13 July casualty snapshot (94 deaths, 1,316 injured, 18 missing) remains the freshest citable figure.

Re-checked 3 August 2026: DSWD DROMIC Report #76 (24 July 2026) remains the latest in its series, with no Report #77 yet published; the OCHA 13 July casualty snapshot (94 deaths, 1,316 injured, 18 missing) remains the freshest citable figure.

DSWD DROMIC Report #77, as of 31 July 2026, 6PM (published on ReliefWeb 3 August 2026), reports 392,389 families (1,657,524 persons) affected across 661 barangays in Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM (unchanged from Report #76). Total displaced: 27,289 families (108,472 persons) -- 7,763 families (31,917 persons) inside 86 evacuation centers (up from 85) and 19,526 families (76,555 persons) staying outside with relatives or friends. Houses damaged: 115,205 total (18,644 totally destroyed, 96,561 partially damaged), unchanged from Report #76. Cost of assistance provided to date: PHP 1,383,697,520.37 (PHP 1,383,677,520.37 from DSWD and PHP 20,000.00 from LGUs), up from PHP 1,306,112,420.37 in Report #76. The report's casualty section still does not carry a death/injured/missing figure.

At least 19 people were killed, 12 remain missing and at least 134 were injured after the 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck Sarangani province on 8 June 2026, according to OCHA, with authorities noting the figures were provisional as assessments continued; more than 3.2 million learners were affected with classes suspended in over 6,200 schools.

By 23 June, government figures reported 77 deaths, with about 1.6 million people affected across Regions IX, XI, XII, and BARMM. PHIVOLCS recorded more than 9,400 aftershocks and further seismic activity expected. More than 80,000 houses have been damaged, including nearly 15,000 destroyed, with 884 damaged infrastructure losses and 130 affected roads and 47 bridges limiting access to isolated communities. Eighteen local government units (LGUs) have declared a state of calamity.

DSWD DROMIC Report #58, as of 09 July 2026, 6AM, reports 391,891 families (1,655,313 persons) affected in 650 barangays across Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM, with 24,097 families (92,256 persons) still displaced — 7,008 families (28,090 persons) inside 74 evacuation centers and 17,089 families (64,166 persons) staying outside evacuation centers with relatives or friends. A total of 121,426 houses were damaged, of which 19,305 were totally destroyed and 102,121 partially damaged.

DSWD DROMIC Report #60, as of 10 July 2026, 6AM, reports 391,871 families (1,655,313 persons) affected in 650 barangays across Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM, with 24,919 families (95,129 persons) still displaced — 7,830 families (30,963 persons) inside 79 evacuation centers and 17,089 families (64,166 persons) staying outside evacuation centers with relatives or friends. A total of 121,307 houses were damaged, of which 19,188 were totally destroyed and 102,119 partially damaged.

DSWD DROMIC Report #64, as of 13 July 2026, 6PM, reports a total of 391,891 families (1,655,313 persons) affected in 650 barangays in Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM. There are 25,048 families (95,629 persons) still displaced in Regions XI, XII and BARMM — 7,959 families (31,463 persons) inside 80 evacuation centers in Regions XI and XII, and 17,089 families (64,166 persons) temporarily staying with relatives or friends. A total of 121,426 houses were damaged, of which 19,305 were totally damaged and 102,121 were partially damaged. A total of ₱1,156,615,547.45 worth of assistance has been provided to affected families, of which ₱1,156,595,547.45 came from DSWD and ₱20,000.00 from LGUs.

DSWD DROMIC Report #66, as of 16 July 2026, 6PM, reports a total of 391,975 families (1,655,686 persons) affected across 651 barangays across Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM. There are 24,472 families (93,971 persons) still displaced — 7,383 families (29,805 persons) inside 78 evacuation centers and 17,089 families (64,166 persons) staying outside evacuation centers with relatives or friends. A total of 121,362 houses were damaged, of which 19,193 were totally destroyed and 102,169 partially damaged.

DSWD DROMIC Report #71, as of 20 July 2026, 6AM, reports a total of 391,975 families (1,655,686 persons) affected across 651 barangays across Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM. There are 24,707 families (94,894 persons) still displaced — 7,618 families (30,728 persons) inside 78 evacuation centers and 17,089 families (64,166 persons) staying outside evacuation centers with relatives or friends. A total of 121,362 houses were damaged, of which 19,193 were totally destroyed and 102,169 partially damaged. Total cost of assistance provided to date is ₱1,284,626,667.47.

DSWD DROMIC Report #72, as of 20 July 2026, 6PM, reports 391,975 families (1,655,686 persons) affected across 651 barangays in Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM (unchanged from Report #71). Total displaced: 24,640 families (94,559 persons) — 7,551 families (30,393 persons) inside 75 evacuation centers, 17,089 families (64,166 persons) outside with relatives/friends. Houses damaged: 121,362 total (19,193 totally damaged, 102,169 partially damaged) — same totals as Report #71. Cost of assistance provided to date: PHP 1,284,768,965.47.

description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck offshore Sarangani province in the southern Philippines on 8 June 2026 (7:37am local time / 7 June 23:37 UTC), triggering a tsunami of nearly 2 metres and widespread damage across Mindanao. GDACS issued an orange alert for medium humanitarian impact. The confirmed death toll has not been revised since an OCHA-produced response snapshot dated 13 July 2026 put it at 94 deaths, 1,316 injured and 18 missing -- DSWD's DROMIC reporting series no longer carries a casualty section -- and eighteen local government units have declared a state of calamity. As of DSWD DROMIC Report #77 (31 July 2026, 6PM, published on ReliefWeb 3 August 2026), 392,389 families (1,657,524 persons) remain recorded as affected across 661 barangays in Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM (unchanged from Report #76), while total displacement eased slightly to 27,289 families (108,472 persons) from 27,508 families (109,445 persons) in Report #76; houses damaged remain unchanged at 115,205 (18,644 totally destroyed, 96,561 partially damaged).

impact.summary: DSWD DROMIC Report #77 (31 July 2026, 6PM, published on ReliefWeb 3 August 2026) reports 392,389 families (1,657,524 persons) affected across 661 barangays in Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM, unchanged from Report #76. Total displacement eased slightly to 27,289 families (108,472 persons) -- 7,763 families (31,917 persons) inside 86 evacuation centers (up from 85) and 19,526 families (76,555 persons) staying outside with relatives or friends -- down from 27,508 families (109,445 persons) as of Report #76. Houses damaged remain unchanged at 115,205 total (18,644 totally destroyed, 96,561 partially damaged). Assistance provided to date totals PHP 1,383,697,520.37 (PHP 1,383,677,520.37 from DSWD and PHP 20,000.00 from LGUs), up from PHP 1,306,112,420.37 as of Report #76. DSWD's DROMIC report template still carries no casualty section, so the most recent citable death/injury/missing figures remain OCHA's 13 July snapshot (94 deaths, 1,316 injured, 18 missing); GDACS assessed an orange alert (medium humanitarian impact) with about 2.9 million people exposed to severe shaking and a tsunami of up to 1.93 metres; eighteen local government units have declared a state of calamity. No allowlisted source has declared the response concluded or resolved. Re-checked 5 August 2026: DSWD DROMIC Report #77 (31 July 2026) is the latest in its series as of this check; the OCHA 13 July casualty snapshot (94 deaths, 1,316 injured, 18 missing) remains the freshest citable figure.
